1 # Variables and Expressions 2 3 Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files. 4 5 > **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow. 6 > 7 > `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors: 8 > 9 > - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107) 10 > - Invented `nodes..output` syntax 11 > - References to unknown variables or node IDs 12 > - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false` 13 > 14 > Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## Table of contents 19 20 - [Variables Overview](#variables-overview) 21 - [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals) 22 - [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes) 23 - [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates) 24 - [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes) 25 - [Expression System](#expression-system) 26 - [Available Globals](#available-globals) 27 - [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts) 28 - [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints) 29 - [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules) 30 - [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli) 31 - [Complete Example](#complete-example) 32 33 --- 34 35 ## Variables Overview 36 37 Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 --- 542 543 ## Scoping Rules 544 545 ### Node Output Availability 546 547 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 548 549 ### Loop Scope 550 551 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 552 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 553 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 554 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 555 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 556 557 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 558 559 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 560 561 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 562 563 ### Subflow Scope 564 565 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 566 567 --- 568 569 ## Variable Management via CLI 570 571 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 572 573 ### Adding a workflow input variable 574 575 1. Open `.flow` 576 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 577 3. Run `uip maestro flow validate` to check for errors 578 579 ### Adding node variables after manual node insertion 580 581 When adding nodes via `Edit` (not CLI), you must also add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`: 582 583 ```json 584 { 585 "id": "myScript.output", 586 "type": "object", 587 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "output" } 588 }, 589 { 590 "id": "myScript.error", 591 "type": "object", 592 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "error" } 593 } 594 ``` 595 596 > **When using `uip maestro flow node add`**, node variables are handled automatically. Only add them manually when using `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 597 598 ### Mapping outputs on End nodes 599 600 For every `out` variable, add a mapping in each End node's `outputs`: 601 602 ```json 603 "outputs": { 604 "result": { 605 "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output" 606 } 607 } 608 ``` 609 610 --- 611 612 ## Complete Example 613 614 A flow with input, state, and output 1	# Index Context (Context Grounding RAG)
2	
3	Walkthrough for adding a context resource backed by an ECS Context Grounding index. Used for RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) — the agent issues queries against the index and gets back relevant chunks.
4	
5	For other context variants, see [context.md](context.md).
6	
7	## When to Use
8	
9	- Agent needs to retrieve from a knowledge base of indexed documents
10	- The index already exists in Context Grounding and is backed by an Orchestrator storage bucket. To create or manage that index from the CLI, see [uipath-platform/references/context-grounding/index-management.md](../../../../../uipath-platform/references/context-grounding/index-management.md)
11	
12	`uip solution resources refresh` emits an `index` binding into `bindings_v2.json`, resolves the backing storage bucket via ECS + Orchestrator, and writes all three artifacts automatically: `resources/solution_folder/index/<IndexName>.json`, `resources/solution_folder/bucket/orchestratorBucket/<BucketName>.json`, and two `debug_overwrites.json` entries (`kind: "index"`, `kind: "bucket"`). No manual solution-level authoring is required.
13	
14	**Only `contextType: "index"` with a StorageBucket data source is supported.** `attachments` and `datafabricentityset` contexts, and indexes backed by GoogleDrive / OneDrive / Dropbox / Confluence, emit a warning from refresh and must be hand-authored.
15	
16	## Discovery
17	
18	Two `uip` calls — identity from `resource list`, full configuration from `resource get`. Symmetric with [../process/process.md § Discovery](../process/process.md#discovery).
19	
20	### Step 1 — Verify login and scaffold (if not already done)
21	
22	Run `uip login status --output json`. If a solution and agent do not yet exist, scaffold per [../../project-lifecycle.md § End-to-End Example](../../project-lifecycle.md#end-to-end-example--new-standalone-agent).
23	
24	### Step 2 — Find the index (identity)
25	
26	```bash
27	uip solution resources list --kind Index --source remote --search "<INDEX_NAME>" --output json
28	```
29	
30	Response wrapper: `{Result, Code: "ResourceList", Data: [...]}` — parse `.Data[]`.
31	
32	| Field | Use as |
33	|-------|--------|
34	| `Key` | index GUID — pass to `resource get` in Step 3. Not stored in the agent resource. |
35	| `Name` | exact `indexName` to set in the context resource → also propagates as binding `name` |
36	| `Folder` | literal folder path → top-level `folderPath` (e.g., `"Shared/Knowledge"`) and binding `folderPath`. Refresh uses `(name, folderPath)` jointly to look up the index in ECS. |
37	| `FolderKey` | folder GUID. Refresh resolves it from `Folder`; informational here. |
38	
39	When the same `Name` repeats across folders, pick by `Key`.
40	
41	### Step 3 — Get the index configuration
42	
43	```bash
44	uip solution resources get <KEY> --output json
45	```
46	
47	Response wrapper: `{Result, Code: "ResourceConfiguration", Data: {...}}`. `Data.spec` is the source-of-truth that `uip solution resources refresh` round-trips into `resources/solution_folder/index/<IndexName>.json` — confirm it before authoring.
48	
49	| `Data.spec` field | Confirms / Use as |
50	|-------|------------------|
51	| `dataSourceType` | MUST equal `"StorageBucket"`. Anything else (GoogleDrive / OneDrive / Dropbox / Confluence / Attachments) — refresh warns + skips. Hand-author solution-level files or escalate. |
52	| `storageBucketReference.name` | Bucket display name. Refresh writes this as the bucket manifest's `name`. Optionally cross-check with `uip solution resources list --kind Bucket --source remote --search "<NAME>" --output json` to confirm the bucket is reachable. |
53	| `storageBucketReference.key` | Bucket GUID — refresh writes this verbatim as `key` in the bucket manifest and as `dependencies[].key` / `spec.storageBucketReference.key` in the index manifest. |
54	| `storageBucketReference.folderKey` | Folder GUID containing the bucket. Matches the index's `FolderKey` from Step 2 (the bucket lives in the same folder as the index). |
55	| `fileNameGlob` | File-extension filter on the index itself. Sanity-check — does not need to match the agent resource's `settings.fileExtension.value`. |
56	| `includeSubfolders`, `ingestionType`, `encrypted` | Reference fields — refresh round-trips them into the solution-level index manifest. |
57	
58	Wrapper-level `apiVersion` is `"ecs.uipath.com/v2"` — matches what refresh writes.
59	
60	## Agent-Level Resource Shape
61	
62	**Path:** `<AgentName>/resources/<ContextName>/resource.json`
63	
64	```jsonc
65	{
66	  "$resourceType": "context",
67	  "id": "<uuid>",                       // stable; generate once
68	  "referenceKey": null,                 // leave null; refresh resolves the ECS index GUID by indexName
69	  "name": "<ContextName>",              // display name; matches the folder under resources/
70	  "description": "",
71	  "contextType": "index",
72	  "folderPath": "Shared/Knowledge",     // Literal Folder from `uip solution resources list`. Propagates verbatim into bindings_v2.json.
73	  "indexName": "<IndexName>",           // MUST match the ECS index Name exactly (case-sensitive)
74	  "settings": {
75	    "retrievalMode": "semantic",        // "semantic" | "structured" | "deeprag" | "batchtransform"
76	    "query": { "variant": "dynamic", "description": "Query for retrieval" },
77	    "folderPathPrefix": { "variant": "static" },
78	    "fileExtension": { "value": "All" },  // object, not string
79	    "threshold": 0,
80	    "resultCount": 3
81	  }
82	}
83	```
84	
85	**`retrievalMode` values (all lowercase) and per-mode `fileExtension.value` + extra fields:**
86	
87	| `retrievalMode` | Legal `fileExtension.value` | Extra required fields |
88	|---|---|---|
89	| `"semantic"` | `"All"`, `"pdf"`, `"csv"`, `"json"`, `"docx"`, `"xlsx"`, `"txt"` | none |
90	| `"structured"` | `"csv"` | none |
91	| `"deeprag"` | `"pdf"`, `"txt"` | `"citationMode": { "value": "Inline" }` (or `"Skip"`) |
92	| `"batchtransform"` | `"csv"` | `"webSearchGrounding": { "value": "Enabled" }` (or `"Disabled"`), `"outputColumns": [{ "name": "...", "description": "..." }, ...]` |
93	
94	**`query.variant`:** `"dynamic"` (LLM supplies at runtime), `"argument"` (bound to an input field), or `"static"` (pre-set value).
95	
96	**`folderPathPrefix.variant`:** `"static"` (no prefix) or `"argument"` (scope by a folder path provided at runtime).
97	
98	**Casing matters.** All `contextType` and `retrievalMode` values are lowercase. See [../../critical-rules/critical-rules.md](../../critical-rules/critical-rules.md) Anti-pattern 12.
99	
100	## Solution-Level Files
101	
102	For `contextType: "index"` with a StorageBucket-backed ECS index, `uip agent refresh` emits:
103	
104	```json
105	{
106	  "resource": "index",
107	  "key": "<IndexName>",
108	  "value": {
109	    "name":       { "defaultValue": "<IndexName>", "isExpression": false, "displayName": "Index Name" },
110	    "folderPath": { "defaultValue": "<Folder>",    "isExpression": false }
111	  },
112	  "metadata": { "bindingsVersion": "2.2", "solutionsSupport": "true" }
113	}
114	```
115	
116	into `bindings_v2.json` at the agent project root. `folderPath` is propagated verbatim from the agent-level `resource.json`'s top-level `folderPath` field. `uip solution resources refresh` then:
117	
118	1. Calls ECS `GET ecs_/v2/indexes/AllAcrossFolders?$filter=Name eq '<IndexName>'&$expand=dataSource` — resolves the index GUID, folder key, and data source type. With the binding's `folderPath` set, refresh narrows multi-folder name collisions to the exact deployment.
119	2. If `dataSource.@odata.type` is not `#UiPath.Vdbs.Domain.Api.V20Models.StorageBucketDataSource`, warns + skips (other data sources — GoogleDrive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Confluence, Attachments — are not yet wired).
120	3. Calls Orchestrator `GET orchestrator_/odata/Buckets?$filter=Name eq '<BucketName>'` with the index's `folderKey` as `X-UIPATH-FolderKey` — gets the bucket `Identifier` GUID.
121	4. Registers the bucket as a solution resource via the resource-builder SDK — writes `resources/solution_folder/bucket/orchestratorBucket/<BucketName>.json`.
122	5. Hand-writes `resources/solution_folder/index/<IndexName>.json` with `kind: "index"`, `apiVersion: "ecs.uipath.com/v2"`, `dependencies: [{name: "<BucketName>", kind: "bucket"}]`, `spec.storageBucketReference: { name, key }`, `dataSourceType: "StorageBucket"`.
123	6. Appends two entries (`kind: "index"` + `kind: "bucket"`) to `userProfile/<userId>/debug_overwrites.json`.
124	
125	All failures (index not found, ambiguous name match, non-StorageBucket data source, bucket missing in Orchestrator) warn + continue — the command never aborts.
126	
127	### Index Definition (refresh fallback)
128	
129	**Path:** `resources/solution_folder/index/{IndexName}.json`
130	
131	```jsonc
132	{
133	  "docVersion": "1.0.0",
134	  "resource": {
135	    "name": "MyIndex",
136	    "kind": "index",
137	    "apiVersion": "ecs.uipath.com/v2",
138	    "isOverridable": true,
139	    "dependencies": [
140	      {
141	        "name": "my_storage_bucket",
142	        "kind": "bucket",
143	        "key": "<bucket-resource-uuid>"
144	      }
145	    ],
146	    "spec": {
147	      "name": "MyIndex",
148	      "description": "",
149	      "storageBucketReference": {
150	        "name": "my_storage_bucket",
151	        "key": "<bucket-resource-uuid>"
152	      },
153	      "fileNameGlob": "All",
154	      "dataSourceType": "StorageBucket",
155	      "includeSubfolders": true,
156	      "ingestionType": "Advanced"
157	    },
158	    "key": "<unique-uuid>"
159	  }
160	}
161	```
162	
163	### Storage Bucket Definition (refresh fallback)
164	
165	**Path:** `resources/solution_folder/bucket/orchestratorBucket/{BucketName}.json`
166	
167	```jsonc
168	{
169	  "docVersion": "1.0.0",
170	  "resource": {
171	    "name": "my_storage_bucket",
172	    "kind": "bucket",
173	    "type": "orchestratorBucket",
174	    "apiVersion": "orchestrator.uipath.com/v1",
175	    "isOverridable": true,
176	    "spec": {
177	      "type": "Orchestrator",
178	      "description": null,
179	      "tags": []
180	    },
181	    "key": "<unique-uuid>"
182	  }
183	}
184	```
185	
186	## Walkthrough
187	
188	### Step 4 — Create the agent-level context resource
189	
190	**Path:** `<AgentName>/resources/<ContextName>/resource.json`
191	
192	```jsonc
193	{
194	  "$resourceType": "context",
195	  "id": "<uuid>",                       // generate a fresh UUID
196	  "referenceKey": null,
197	  "name": "<ContextName>",
198	  "description": "",
199	  "contextType": "index",
200	  "folderPath": "<FOLDER>",             // literal Folder from Step 2 (e.g., "Shared/Knowledge")
201	  "indexName": "<INDEX_NAME>",          // exact ECS index name from Step 2
202	  "settings": {
203	    "retrievalMode": "semantic",
204	    "query": { "variant": "dynamic" },
205	    "folderPathPrefix": { "variant": "static" },
206	    "fileExtension": { "value": "All" },
207	    "threshold": 0,
208	    "resultCount": 3
209	  }
210	}
211	```
212	
213	See § Agent-Level Resource Shape above for the full field reference, including the three variants (`index`/`attachments`/`datafabricentityset`) and per-`retrievalMode` settings (`citationMode` for `deeprag`, `webSearchGrounding` + `outputColumns` for `batchtransform`).
214	
215	### Step 4b — Inline agents only: wire the context flow node
216	
217	**Skip if the agent is standalone.** If the context is on an **inline** agent (embedded in a flow), the `resource.json` alone is never reached at runtime — you MUST also add a `uipath.agent.resource.context.index.<index-name>.<index-id>` flow node connected to the autonomous node's `context` handle (bottom port). Fetch its manifest with `uip maestro flow registry get "<NodeType>" --output json`, then hand the node + edge authoring to the `uipath-maestro-flow` skill (Critical Rule 16 — this skill does not author `.flow` graphs directly). Run Step 5's refresh/validate with `--inline-in-flow` plus `--bindings-target <FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json`. See [../inline-in-flow/inline-in-flow.md](../inline-in-flow/inline-in-flow.md).
218	
219	### Step 5 — Refresh and validate
220	
221	```bash
222	uip agent refresh  "<AGENT_NAME>" --output json
223	uip agent validate "<AGENT_NAME>" --output json
224	```
225	
226	Refresh writes the binding. Validate is read-only. Confirm `Validated.resources` includes the context, then inspect the emitted binding:
227	
228	```bash
229	cat "<AGENT_NAME>/bindings_v2.json"
230	# Expect: resources[0] with {resource: "index", key: "<INDEX_NAME>", ...}
231	```
232	
233	### Step 6 — Refresh solution resources
234	
235	```bash
236	uip solution resources refresh --output json
237	```
238	
239	Refresh resolves the index via ECS `$expand=dataSource`, locates its backing StorageBucket in Orchestrator, and writes:
240	
241	- `resources/solution_folder/index/<INDEX_NAME>.json` — manifest with `kind: "index"`, `apiVersion: "ecs.uipath.com/v2"`, `dependencies: [{name, kind: "bucket"}]`, `spec.storageBucketReference.{name,key}`.
242	- `resources/solution_folder/bucket/orchestratorBucket/<BucketName>.json` — standard bucket manifest.
243	- `userProfile/<userId>/debug_overwrites.json` — two entries (`kind: "index"` and `kind: "bucket"`), both referencing the index's folder.
244	
245	Check the `Warnings` array in the refresh output. Common warnings:
246	- `Index "<NAME>" not found in ECS` — exact-name mismatch. Re-check the index name.
247	- `Index uses <type>, which is not yet supported` — data source is GoogleDrive/OneDrive/Dropbox/Confluence/Attachments; hand-author the solution-level files. Step 3's `dataSourceType` check should have caught this earlier.
248	- `Storage bucket "<NAME>" not found in Orchestrator folder` — the bucket was deleted or lives in a different folder than the index.
249	
250	### Step 7 — Bundle and upload
251	
252	```bash
253	uip solution bundle . -d ./dist --output json
254	uip solution upload ./dist/<SOLUTION_NAME>.uis --output json
255	```
256	
257	The upload response includes a `Data.DesignerUrl` — open it to verify the context appears wired to the ECS index in Studio Web.
258	
259	## Gotchas
260	
261	`contextType` and `retrievalMode` values MUST be lowercase — see [../../critical-rules/critical-rules.md](../../critical-rules/critical-rules.md) Anti-pattern 12.
262	
263	## References
264	
265	- [context.md](context.md) — capability overview and variant decision
266	- [attachments.md](attachments.md) — runtime file attachments
267	- [datafabric.md](datafabric.md) — DataFabric entity-set context
268	- [../../solution-resources.md](../../solution-resources.md) § Refresh Mechanics

commands.result_summary:
1	# Connector Activity Nodes — Implementation
2	
3	How to configure connector activity nodes: connection binding, enriched metadata, reference field resolution, and debugging. Connection bindings are emitted by `uip maestro flow node configure` into the flow's top-level `bindings[]`; `bindings_v2.json` is regenerated from them at debug/pack time and should never be hand-edited.
4	
5	For generic node/edge add, remove, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). This guide covers the connector-specific configuration workflow that must follow the generic node add.
6	
7	## How Connector Nodes Differ from OOTB
8	
9	1. **Connection binding required** — every connector node needs an IS connection (OAuth, API key, etc.) authored in the flow's top-level `bindings[]` (which the CLI regenerates into `bindings_v2.json` at debug/pack time). Without it, the node cannot authenticate.
10	2. **Enriched metadata via `--connection-id`** — call `registry get` with `--connection-id` to get connection-aware field metadata. Without it, only base fields are returned — custom fields, dynamic enums, and reference resolution are missing.
11	3. **`inputs.detail` object** — connector nodes store operation-specific configuration in `inputs.detail`, populated by `uip maestro flow node configure`:
12	   - `connectionId` — the bound IS connection UUID
13	   - `connectionFolderKey` — the Orchestrator folder key in the authored `.flow` file. `node configure --detail` accepts `folderKey` as input and writes it back as `connectionFolderKey`.
14	   - `method` — HTTP method from `registry get` → `connectorMethodInfo.method` (e.g., `POST`)
15	   - `endpoint` — API path. Read `connectorMethodInfo.path` (from `registry get`) or `availableOperations[].path` (from `is resources describe`).
16	   - `objectName` — required for generic activities (see below). The API object name (e.g. `"Opportunity"`); ignored for concrete nodes.
17	   - `bodyParameters` — field-value pairs for the request body. Read field names from `inputDefinition.fields[].name` (`registry get`) or `requestFields[].name` (`is resources describe`).
18	   - `queryParameters` — field-value pairs for query string parameters. Read from `connectorMethodInfo.parameters[]` where `type: query` (`registry get`) or `parameters[]` (`is resources describe`).
19	   - `pathParameters` — field-value pairs for path placeholders in `endpoint` (e.g. `{conversationsInfoId}`). Read from `connectorMethodInfo.parameters[]` where `type: path` (`registry get`) or `parameters[]` (`is resources describe`).
20	   - `filter` — structured FilterBuilder tree for list/query operations. See Step 6a.
21	   - `customFieldsRequestDetails` — design-time cache for connectors with an api-type ObjectAction at top-level `objectActions[]` OR `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` (e.g. Jira `GenerateSchema`, Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant`). camelCase keys; `parameterValues` as `[key, value]` tuples. See Step 6c.
22	   - `multipartParameters` — derived from IS metadata params where `type === "multipart"`. Array of `{name, dataType, value?}`. Pass file values via `--detail.bodyParameters.<name>`; `node configure` moves file-typed values into the matching `multipartParameters[i].value` slot (matched by `name`). String-typed entries — including the body aggregator field whose name is given by `inputMetadata.multipart.bodyFieldName` — stay in `bodyParameters`.
23	   - `inputMetadata` — auto-derived. `{type: "multipart", multipart: {bodyFieldName}}` when multipart params exist; `{operation: "list", pagination: {maxPageSize}}` for list operations. Driven by `methodInfo.parameters` + `methodInfo.operation`.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Generic vs Concrete Activities
28	
29	Connector nodes come in two flavors:
30	
31	- **Concrete** — the node type encodes a specific object + operation (e.g. `uipath.connector.uipath-atlassian-jira.curated_create_issue`). `inputDefinition.fields[]` is populated; `method` and `endpoint` are fixed.
32	- **Generic** — the node type encodes only the operation (e.g. `uipath.connector.uipath-salesforce-sfdc.list-records`, `…insert-record`, `…update-record`). `inputDefinition` is `{}`; the node needs an extra `objectName` in `--detail`, and `method` / `endpoint` come from `is resources describe`.
33	
34	To classify a node, read `Node.form.sections[0].fields[0].componentProps.connectorDetail.configuration` from the `registry get` response, parse it as JSON, and check `activityType`. `"Generic"` → run Step 2a to discover `objectName` (and capture `operation` from the same marker for the `--operation` flag in Step 3). Anything else → skip Step 2a.
35	
36	
37	## Critical: Connector Definition Must Include `form`
38	
39	> Connector definitions in `definitions[]` are CLI-owned (see [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node)) — `uip maestro flow node add` copies them verbatim from the registry, and you should never hand-write or hand-edit them. If `node configure` fails with `No instanceParameters found in definition`, the definition in `definitions[]` is missing the `form` field — typically because the local registry cache is stale (the definition was copied in before the CLI started emitting `form`). Recovery: `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`, delete the stale `definitions[]` entry, re-run `uip maestro flow node add <file> <node-type>` so the CLI re-copies the definition with `form`. Do not paste `form` in by hand — re-running `node add` is the supported path.
40	
41	## No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration
42	
43	If you cannot run `node configure` (no live connection, sandbox forbids it, the user asked for planning only):
44	
45	1. Confirm the connector operation exists: `uip maestro flow registry search <keyword>` and `registry get <node-type>` (see [cli-commands.md — registry](../../../../shared/cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-registry) for the `search` output shape).
46	2. Add the connector node with `uip maestro flow node add <file> <node-type> --output json`. This is still required — it inserts the node and copies the definition into `definitions[]`.
47	3. Write the planned `--detail` payload to a separate file (e.g. `<nodeId>.detail.json`) with placeholder values for missing connection/folder UUIDs. Do **not** put a partial `inputs.detail` on the node.
48	4. **The node will not pass `flow validate` until `node configure` is run.** Surface this explicitly in your completion report under "Missing connections" or "Open questions" — do not let the user discover it via a validation failure later.
49	
50	Do not replace a registered connector operation with `core.logic.mock` because configuration cannot run. Mocks are only for genuinely unknown, unpublished, or not-yet-built non-connector resources. A real connector node added via `node add` but unconfigured preserves the registered connector key that Studio Web, reviewers, and downstream tooling need.
51	
52	When piping `--output json` into `python`, `jq`, or another parser, do not merge stderr into stdout. The CLI may emit diagnostic lines such as "Tool factory already registered..." before the JSON on stderr; use `2>/dev/null` for parse-only probes or capture stderr separately.
53	
54	## Configuration Workflow
55	
56	Follow these steps for every connector node.
57	
58	### Step 1 — Fetch and bind a connection
59	
60	Extract the connector key from the node type (`uipath.connector.<connector-key>.<activity-name>`).
61	
62	Discovery call is **always**:
63	
64	```bash
65	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
66	```
67	
68	`connections list` returns `Data` as a flat array. Do **not** parse `Data.Connections` or `Data.Items`; those wrapper objects are not part of the CLI JSON contract. Read each candidate from `Data[]` and use PascalCase fields:
69	
70	```json
71	{
72	  "Data": [
73	    {
74	      "Id": "<connection-id>",
75	      "Name": "<display-name>",
76	      "State": "Enabled",
77	      "IsDefault": "Yes",
78	      "Folder": "<folder-name>",
79	      "FolderKey": "<folder-key>"
80	    }
81	  ]
82	}
83	```
84	
85	Use `Data[i].Id` as the `--connection-id` value and `Data[i].FolderKey` as the `folderKey` value in `node configure --detail`.
86	
87	> **MUST READ before any `uip is connections ...` call:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md). Single source of truth for selection rules (auto-select, personal workspace), BYOA filtering, empty-result recovery, ping verification.
88	
89	End state: a healthy connection `Id` + `FolderKey` for Step 2 (`registry get --connection-id`) and Step 6 (`node configure --detail`).
90	
91	### Step 2 — Get enriched node definitions with connection
92	
93	Call `registry get` with `--connection-id` to fetch connection-aware metadata including custom fields:
94	
95	```bash
96	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --connection-id <connection-id> --output json
97	```
98	
99	This returns enriched `inputDefinition.fields` and `outputDefinition.fields` with accurate type, required, description, enum, and `reference` info. Without `--connection-id`, only standard/base fields are returned.
100	
101	The response also includes `connectorMethodInfo` with the real HTTP `method` (e.g. `GET`, `POST`) and `path` template (e.g. `/ConversationsInfo/{conversationsInfoId}`). **Save `connectorMethodInfo.method` and `connectorMethodInfo.path`** — you must pass them to `node configure` later as `method` and `endpoint`.
102	
103	> **For generic activities, `connectorMethodInfo` is empty.** Method and endpoint are object-specific and only resolve once Step 2a picks an `objectName`; Step 3 then surfaces them via `availableOperations[]`. Don't try to derive them from the manifest alone.
104	
105	### Step 2a — Discover the object name (generic activities only)
106	
107	Skip this step for concrete activities — they encode the object in the node type. For generic activities (`activityType: "Generic"`), list the connection's catalog and pick the object the user wants to act on.
108	
109	```bash
110	uip is resources list "<connector-key>" --connection-id "<connection-id>" --output json \
111	  --output-filter "[?contains(DisplayName,'<search>')].{Name:Name,Path:Path,Custom:Custom}"
112	```
113	
114	- `Name` — what `--detail.objectName` accepts. Case-sensitive (e.g. `"Opportunity"`, not `"opportunity"`). Don't substitute `DisplayName`.
115	- `Path` — API endpoint suffix (e.g. `/Opportunity`). Pair with the operation's HTTP method (Step 3) for `endpoint`.
116	- `Custom` — `true` for tenant-defined objects.
117	
118	### Step 3 — Describe the resource and read full metadata
119	
120	Run `is resources describe` to fetch and cache the full operation metadata, then **read the cached metadata file** for complete field details including descriptions, types, references, and query/path parameters. The describe summary omits some of this.
121	
122	**Read `<objectName>` from the node definition in `definitions[]` (written by `node add`) — do not guess it from the node-type suffix.**
123	
124	```bash
125	# 1. Describe to trigger fetch + cache (objectName = the activity's API object, NOT the node-type suffix)
126	#    Read <objectName> from the node definition FIRST (see note below) — do not batch this
127	#    call with `node add` / `registry get`; those calls PRODUCE the objectName this one consumes.
128	uip is resources describe "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" \
129	  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create --output json
130	# -> response includes metadataFile path
131	
132	# 2. Read the full cached metadata
133	cat <metadataFile path from response>
134	```
135	
136	> **`<objectName>` is the activity's API object name, not the node-type's trailing segment — and NOT a case-conversion of it.** Read it from the node definition copied into `definitions[]` by `node add`: `model.context[]` entry `{name:"objectName", value:"…"}` (or the `objectName` field inside the `configuration` `=jsonString:` blob). Never derive it by transforming the node-type suffix — kebab→snake (`send-email` → `send_email`) and kebab→Pascal are both guesses and both 404. Example: node type `…google-gmail.send-email` has objectName `SendEmail` (not `send_email`); `…teams.send-bot-direct-message` has objectName `bot_direct_messages` (not `send-bot-direct-message`). A 404 means wrong objectName — re-read it from the definition and retry; do NOT treat the 404 as "describe unavailable" and skip the step. Skipping describe loses `requestFields[].reference.filterPattern` and other IS-level metadata that `registry get` does not carry (see Step 4).
137	>
138	> **Sequence, don't parallelize, the objectName-dependent calls.** `<objectName>` is an OUTPUT of `node add` (it lands in `definitions[]`). Read that value before calling `is resources describe` — do not place `describe` in the same parallel Bash batch as `node add` or `registry get`, or you'll have nothing to pass but a guess. This is the failure mode behind the snake-case 404 above.
139	
140	The full metadata contains:
141	- **`availableOperations[].method`** and **`availableOperations[].path`** — HTTP method and API endpoint path. Same value as `connectorMethodInfo.method` / `.path` from `registry get`.
142	- **`parameters`** — query and path parameters (may include required params not in `requestFields`, e.g. `send_as` for Slack)
143	- **`requestFields`** — body fields with `name`, `type`, `required`, `description`, and `reference` objects for ID resolution. Pair these field names with the `path` above (e.g. `messageToSend` for Slack `/send_message_to_channel_v2`).
144	- **`responseFields`** — response schema
145	
146	### Step 3a — Resolve parent-field-driven custom fields (api-type ObjectActions)
147	
148	**Run whenever the activity has a parent-field-driven schema** — an api-type ObjectAction in `objectActions[]` or `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` (see Step 6c's support table). Applies to **every** operation with such an action — Create/Edit/Update for parent-driven required body fields AND Get/Retrieve/Query for the response-schema fields downstream nodes will reference. The base `describe` returns only static metadata; this step runs the matching ObjectAction against the live connection so the cache you author in Step 6c is a replay of a real call, not a fabrication.
149	
150	Pass parent values via `-f, --field` — see [/uipath:uipath-platform — resources.md > Parent-Field-Driven Custom Fields (api-type ObjectActions)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md#parent-field-driven-custom-fields-api-type-objectactions) for the full procedure, flag table, merge semantics, and error recovery.

154	Run this before Step 5 (validate required fields) and reuse the same parent-field values in Step 6c's `customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues` (with the encoded keys).

156	### Step 4 — Resolve reference fields
157	
158	Check `requestFields` from the metadata for fields with a `reference` object — these require ID lookup from the connector's live data. Use `uip is resources run list` to resolve them:
159	
160	> **Resolve every reference field freshly, against the current `--connection-id`, immediately before `node configure` (Step 6)** — even if you think you already know the ID from a previous flow. Reference IDs are connection-scoped and reused values fault silently at runtime. See [Reference IDs Are Connection-Scoped (CRITICAL)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/reference-resolution.md#reference-ids-are-connection-scoped-critical) for the full mechanism and failure mode, and the top-level Anti-Patterns in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md).
161	
162	```bash
163	# Example: resolve Slack channel "#test-slack" to its ID
164	uip is resources run list "uipath-salesforce-slack" "curated_channels?types=public_channel,private_channel" \
165	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
166	# -> { "id": "C1234567890", "name": "test-slack" }
167	```
168	
169	The `<id>` in `--connection-id "<id>"` MUST be the connection bound to **this** flow (the one picked in Step 1), not any other connection you've used in another flow. Use the resolved IDs (not display names) — from this very `run list` call — in the flow's node `inputs`. When multiple matches exist, ask the user, with one option per match plus **"Something else"** as the last option (see the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md)).
170	
171	> **Filter server-side before paginating.** If the field's `reference` carries a `filterPattern` (e.g. Teams `userId`: `"$filter=startswith(userPrincipalName,'{filter}')"`), substitute the search term for `{filter}` and pass the result as `--query` — one targeted call instead of walking a large directory. `filterPattern` appears only in `is resources describe` output; the flow `registry get` reference object strips it (keeps only `objectName`/`lookupValue`/`lookupNames`/`path`/`childPath`), so read it from the Step 3 describe metadata. Guessed params (`searchTerm=`/`where=`/`filter=`) are silently ignored. See [reference-resolution.md — Search References (filterPattern)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/reference-resolution.md#search-references-filterpattern).
172	
173	> **Paginate only when there is no `filterPattern`.** Use `Data.Pagination.HasMore` / `NextPageToken` with `--query "nextPage=<token>"`. Short-circuit on match. Do NOT conclude "not found" until `HasMore` is `"false"`. See [resources.md#pagination](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md#pagination).
174	
175	**Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — Integration Service — resources.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md) for the full reference-resolution workflow** (pagination, describe failures, fallbacks).
176	
177	### Step 5 — Validate required fields
178	
179	**Check every required field** — both `requestFields` and `parameters` where `required: true` — against what the user provided. This is a hard gate — do NOT proceed to building until all required fields have values. For query/path parameters with a `defaultValue`, use the default if the user didn't specify one.
180	
181	1. Collect all required fields from the metadata (`requestFields` + `parameters`)
182	2. For each required field, check if the user's prompt contains a value
183	3. If any required field is missing and has no `defaultValue`, **ask the user** before proceeding — list the missing fields with their `displayName` and what kind of value is expected. Free-form input is appropriate when the value space is open-ended (channel names, message bodies, IDs); when a finite set of sensible values exists, present them as options per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md).
184	4. Only after all required fields are accounted for, proceed to building
185	
186	> **Do NOT guess or skip missing required fields.** A missing required field will cause a runtime error. It is always better to ask than to assume.
187	
188	> **For connectors with api-type ObjectActions, run Step 3a first.** Base `describe` does not surface custom required fields driven by project / issue type / query / tenant entity. Use `-f, --field name=value` to fetch the connection-and-parent-field-specific schema before validating.
189	
190	### Step 5b — Wire outputs from previous nodes
191	
192	When a connector node's input field needs a value produced by an upstream node (e.g. the `Id` returned by a Create activity becomes the `recordId` for a Get-by-Id activity), the value MUST use the canonical expression form:
193	
194	```
195	"=js:$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output.<field>"
196	```
197	
198	Examples in `inputs.detail`:
199	
200	```jsonc
201	"queryParameters": {
202	  "recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"
203	},
204	"bodyParameters": {
205	  "ParentId":  "=js:$vars.queryAccounts1.output[0].Id",
206	  "BankName":  "HDFC Bank",
207	  "Note":      "=js:`Linked from run ${$metadata.instanceId}`"
208	}

There is no `nodes.X.output.Y` syntax — that is an invention that silently ships as a literal string. See [node-output-wiring.md](../../../../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the per-field-type rule and the full failure-mode table (MST-9107).
212	
213	### Step 6 — Configure the node
214	
215	**Run `is resources describe` (Step 3) before this step.** The full metadata tells you which fields are required, what types they expect, and which need reference resolution. 216	
217	> **Re-configure is full rebuild, not partial merge — every `--detail` field omitted gets dropped.** Each `node configure` call constructs a fresh `inputs.detail` object (`connector-service.ts:792-803`) and a fresh `essentialConfiguration` blob from `--detail` only. Anything not in this call's `--detail` is dropped from the rewritten flow:
218	>
219	> | If you omit on re-configure | What happens |
220	> |---|---|
221	> | `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` | Field is removed from `inputs.detail` (the prior values are NOT preserved) |
222	> | `filter` | `savedFilterTrees` is omitted from the `=jsonString:` blob; `queryParameters.<filterParamName>` is not re-derived |
223	> | `customFieldsRequestDetails` | Resets to `null` inside the `=jsonString:` blob |
224	>

226

254

256

269	  --detail '{"connectionId": "<id>", "folderKey": "<key>", "method": "GET", "endpoint": "/Opportunity", "objectName": "Opportunity"}' \
270	  --output json

274	
275	```bash
276	uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> \
277	  --detail '{"connectionId": "<id>", "folderKey": "<key>", "method": "GETBYID", "endpoint": "/Account/{accountId}", "objectName": "Account", "pathParameters": {"accountId": "001KY000007uI02YAE"}}' \
278	  --output json
279	```
280	
281	Path-parameterized GETs are a distinct shape from list/query: `endpoint` carries `{<placeholder>}` tokens and `pathParameters` supplies the values. Resolve the ID via `is resources run list <connector-key> <objectName>` (Step 4) — never paste IDs across connections (see [reference-resolution.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/reference-resolution.md#reference-ids-are-connection-scoped-critical)).

283	The `objectName` field is required for generic nodes (see "Generic vs Concrete Activities" above). The CLI fails fast with a runnable hint when it's missing on a generic node. For concrete nodes the field is ignored if supplied.

286	
287	- `registry get` (Step 2) → `connectorMethodInfo.method` and `connectorMethodInfo.path` — populated for **concrete** activities only.
288	- `is resources describe <connector-key> <objectName> --operation <Op>` (Step 3) → `availableOperations[].method` and `availableOperations[].path` — works for both, and is the only source for **generic** activities.
289	
290	> **Method label — pass the IS describe value verbatim.** `is resources describe` sometimes returns synthesized IS-side labels (notably `"GETBYID"` for path-parameterized retrieve operations). The CLI accepts both standard HTTP verbs (`GET`, `POST`, …) and IS-side labels (`GETBYID`) — copy `operation.method` from `is resources describe` as-is and the CLI normalizes to the underlying HTTP verb internally. Don't translate by hand.
291	
292	> **`flow validate` cross-checks `method` against the activity's `operation`.** If the value you pass disagrees with the operation baked into the node by `node add` (e.g. `method: "POST"` on a Retrieve activity), validate fails with `HTTP method "<X>" does not match operation "<Y>". Expected "<Z>"`. This catches stale copy-paste — fix by re-reading `operation.method` from `is resources describe` against the right `--operation`.
293	
294	Body field names in `bodyParameters` come from `inputDefinition.fields[].name` (`registry get`, concrete only) or `requestFields[].name` (`is resources describe`, both).
295	
296	> **Array fields — `[*]` indicates an array.** `[*]` in `requestFields[].name` (or `inputDefinition.fields[].name`) marks the field as an array; `dataType` identifies the element type. **Supported only when `[*]` is the name suffix.** Any name containing `[*].` (path segments after the `[*]`, e.g. `addresses[*].zipCode`, `contacts[*].emails[*]`) is not authorable — the canvas UI does not emit these shapes. The rule below covers `bodyParameters`, `queryParameters`, and `pathParameters`.
297	>
298	> | `requestFields[].name` | `dataType` | Authoring shape in `inputs.detail` |
299	> |---|---|---|
300	> | `fields.labels[*]` | `string` | `"fields.labels": ["shield", "p0"]` |
301	> | `fields.components_arrayRemap_name[*]` | `string` | `"fields.components_arrayRemap_name": ["IS Runtime"]` |
302	>
303	> **Strip `[*]` from the key; pass an array value in `--detail`.** The canvas UI is the source of truth — it omits `[*]` from the wire key on write, and the CLI follows the same convention when it builds `inputs.detail`. The runtime rejects any key containing the literal `[*]` substring as unknown (regardless of value shape), so pass the stripped form in your `node configure --detail` payload. **Distinct from `customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues`**, where `[*]` is encoded as `_array` — see Step 6c.
304	>
305	> **Expression values.** The serializer is purely structural (dot-expansion only; no expression evaluation, no type coercion). Choose the authoring shape based on what the expression returns at runtime:
306	>
307	> | Expression resolves to | Authoring shape | Example |
308	> |---|---|---|
309	> | The whole array | `"<field>": "=<expr>"` | `"fields.labels": "=js:$vars.allTags"` |
310	> | A single element to wrap | `"<field>": ["=<expr>"]` | `"fields.labels": ["=js:$vars.priorityTag"]` |
311	
312	The command populates `inputs.detail` and creates workflow-level `bindings` entries. Use **resolved IDs** from Step 4, not display names. For FilterBuilder params, see Step 6a.
313	
314	When inspecting the resulting `.flow`, note that the folder field is named `connectionFolderKey` in `inputs.detail`. The CLI `--detail` input accepts `folderKey` for convenience, then serializes the `.flow` field expected by validation. Do not hand-edit this field — `inputs.detail` is CLI-owned (see [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node)); re-run `node configure` to change it.
315	
316	> **Do not use `filterExpression`** — that field is the trigger / JMESPath path. See [connector-trigger/impl.md](../connector-trigger/impl.md#filter-trees).
317	
318	> **Shell quoting tip:** For complex `--detail` JSON, write it to a temp file: `uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> --detail "$(cat /tmp/detail.json)" --output json`
319	
320	#### Step 6c — Populate custom fields (api-type ObjectActions)
321	
322	A connector activity has a **parent-field-driven schema** when its valid input fields are not fixed in static metadata but are computed at design time by running an api-type ObjectAction against the IS Element Service. Examples: Jira's `Create Issue` schema depends on the project + issue type; Snowflake's `executeQuery` response columns depend on the SQL string; Dataservice V3's entity field set depends on `tenantEntityName`. The activity persists the parent-field values in `essentialConfiguration.customFieldsRequestDetails` so the runtime can replay the schema-fetch ObjectAction on each invocation. The CLI passes this through verbatim.
323	
324	**How DAP determines support — check both metadata locations.** An api-type action may live at either:
325	
326	- Top-level `objectActions[]` with PascalCase `ActionType: "Api"` (older shape, e.g. Jira `GenerateSchema`)
327	- `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` with lowercase `actionType: "api"` (newer shape, e.g. Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant`)
328	
329	The dispatcher matches `ObjectActionType.Api === 'api'` (case-sensitive lowercase string) — both shapes go through the same `_processCustomFieldsRequestAction` code path with no per-connector branching. Always inspect both locations from `registry get` output before deciding the connector has none.
330	
331	The matching action is then selected by one of two rule sources:
332	
333	- **`source: field`** — the action's `rules[].refFieldName` are satisfied by user-supplied `-f, --field` values (typically SQL-style query connectors where the query string is the parent field).
334	- **`source: method`** — the action is declared at the operation level and matched against the operation's HTTP method (typically CRUD activities).
335	
336	**Examples of supported activities.** The list below is illustrative, not exhaustive — DAP's actual support set evolves with connector metadata. Always confirm by inspecting `objectActions[]` / `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` from `registry get` for the specific (connector, object, activity) you're configuring.
337	
338	| Connector key | Object | Activity / Action | HTTP | Source |
339	|---|---|---|---|---|
340	| `uipath-microsoft-azureapplicationinsights` | `executeQuery` | `generateSchema` | — | field |
341	| `uipath-salesforce-sfdc` | `curated_soqlQuery` | `generateSchema` | — | field |
342	| `uipath-workday-workdayrest` | `wql` | `generateSchema` | — | field |

344	| `uipath-snowflake-snowflake` | `executeQuery` | `generateSchema` | — | field |
345	| `uipath-atlassian-jira` | `curated_create_issue` | Create Issue | POST | method |
346	| `uipath-atlassian-jira` | `curated_edit_issue` | Update Issue | PUT | method |

359	**Token encoding rule.** Tokens are encoded via `NamingHelper.getValidIdentifier` (the IS-side identifier sanitizer) before being used as `parameterValues` keys, so they match design-property names at lookup time. Substitutions (applied longest-first):
360	
361	| Match in token | Encoded as |
362	|---|---|
363	| `:::` | `_sub_` |
364	| `[*]` | `_array` |
365	| `::` | `_sub_` |
366	| `.` | `_sub_` |
367	
368	Examples: `fields.project.key` → `fields_sub_project_sub_key`; `items[*]` → `items_array`; `tenantEntityName` → `tenantEntityName` (unchanged). When in doubt, inspect a working `.flow` for the encoded form.
369	
370	> **`customFieldsRequestDetails` is COMPLEMENTARY to `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters`, not a substitute.** Same parent-field values must appear in BOTH places, with different keys:
371	>
372	> | Location | Purpose | Key shape |
373	> |---|---|---|
374	> | `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` | Runtime input — what the connector actually sends to its API | **Raw** field names (e.g. `fields.project.key`, `tenantEntityName`) |
375	> | `essentialConfiguration.customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues` | Design-time replay cache — drives the parent-field-driven schema fetch when the activity is re-opened or re-validated | **Encoded** keys (e.g. `fields_sub_project_sub_key`, `tenantEntityName`) |
376	>
377	> Concrete (Jira Create Issue): `bodyParameters.fields.project.key = "ENGCE"` AND `parameterValues = [["fields_sub_project_sub_key", "ENGCE"]]`. Concrete (Dataservice V3): `queryParameters.tenantEntityName = ""my-entity""` AND `parameterValues = [["tenantEntityName", ""my-entity""]]`. Dropping the runtime-input copy on the assumption that the cache covers it leaves the runtime with no field value to bind — manifests as `DAP-DT-_2003 refField with name <X> not found` at activity load.

381	```json
382	"customFieldsRequestDetails": {

384	  "parameterValues": [

386	    ["fields_sub_issuetype_sub_id", "3"]
387	  ]

503	
504	## Bindings — top-level `.flow` `bindings[]`
505	
506	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. Bindings are authored in the flow's **top-level `bindings[]` array** (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`). At `flow debug` / `flow pack` time the CLI regenerates `content/bindings_v2.json` from these entries.
507	
508	> **Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly.** Any manual edits are overwritten on the next debug/pack. All authoring flows through the `.flow` file's top-level `bindings[]`.
509	
510	### How connector nodes reference bindings
511	
512	The connector node's **definition** (the manifest copied from `uip maestro flow registry get` into `definitions[]`) carries a `model.context[]` template like this. **Leave the definition exactly as the registry returns it** — do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the definition, and do NOT author `model.context[]` on the instance:
513	
514	```json
515	"context": [
516	  { "name": "connectorKey", "type": "string", "value": "uipath-atlassian-jira" },
517	  { "name": "connection", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.uipath-atlassian-jira connection>" },
518	  { "name": "folderKey", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.FolderKey>" }
519	]
520	```
521	
522	At BPMN emit time, the runtime rewrites each `<bindings.{name}>` placeholder to `=bindings.{id}` by finding a top-level `bindings[]` entry whose `name` matches the placeholder. For connectors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is typically unset, so matching is **name-only** within the `resource: "Connection"` candidate set.
523	
524	> **Matching differs from resource nodes.** For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is set to `<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>`, so placeholder matching is scoped by `(name, resourceKey)`. For connector nodes, `resourceKey` on the definition is typically unset, so matching is name-only — the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder must be unique per connector in the flow. Don't confuse the two patterns.
525	
526	### Top-level `bindings[]` shape (CLI-emitted; reference only)

528	`uip maestro flow node configure` populates these entries — you do not author them by hand. 3:This plugin covers **flow-specific** operations for inline agent nodes: adding the node, wiring edges, JSON structure, and flow validation. For agent-side concerns (agent.json configuration, resource.json authoring, solution resources, prompts), see the `uipath-agents` skill — specifically `lowcode/capabilities/inline-in-flow/inline-in-flow.md`.
227:An inline agent attaches resource nodes — tools (external or built-in), contexts, and escalations — to its three artifact ports. **All kinds wire into the `.flow` identically:** discover the node type, add a minimal node instance, copy its definition into `definitions[]`, add a placeholder layout entry, wire ONE artifact edge to the node's `input` port, then hand-author `resource.json` and run refresh + validate. Three things vary per kind — the **artifact port** the edge leaves, the **node type**, and whether the resource needs **solution-level files**. The `resource.json` body is owned by the `uipath-agents` skill (linked per row).
229:| Kind | Edge source port | Node type | `resource.json` discriminator | Needs `uip solution resources refresh`? | `resource.json` reference (uipath-agents) |
236:| Context (index / RAG) | `context` (bottom) | `uipath.agent.resource.context.index.<index-name>.<index-id>` | `$resourceType: "context"`, `contextType: "index"` | Yes | `lowcode/capabilities/context/index.md` |
237:| Escalation (HITL) | `escalation` (top) | `uipath.agent.resource.escalation` | `$resourceType: "escalation"` | Yes | `lowcode/capabilities/escalation/escalation.md` |
252:# One resource UUID — used as both inputs.source and the resource.json directory/id
256:`<release-key>` is the resource's release-key GUID from `uip solution resources list` (the row's `Key`). `<toolType>` is the built-in's fixed kebab discriminator (e.g. `analyze-attachments`), identical to the `resource.json` `properties.toolType`.
289:### 3. Author `resource.json`
291:Hand-author `<FlowProjectDir>/<inlineAgentProjectId>/resources/<RES_UUID>/resource.json` using the matrix reference for the kind. Set `id` to `<RES_UUID>` (= the node's `inputs.source` and the resource directory name). A `resource.json` missing its `$resourceType` (or `type` for built-ins) is not recognized by `uip agent validate` — it reports `"resources": 0`, and the next refresh writes an empty `bindings_v2.json`.
293:**Process / agent / api / processOrchestration tools** share one shape — use the exact shape in the `uipath-agents` skill: `lowcode/capabilities/process/process.md` § Tool resource.json Shape (read it first). The subtype is the `type` field (§ Subtypes in `process.md`). RPA uses raw .NET arrays (Template A in `solution-files.md`); Agent / API / Process Orchestration use JSON Schema V2 (Template B). Run `uip solution resources list` + `uip solution resources get` to populate `referenceKey`, `folderPath`, `inputSchema`, `outputSchema`. Inline-in-flow specifics:
315:- **Verify both refresh and validate report `"resources": N` where N > 0.** If either shows `"resources": 0`, the `resource.json` is malformed or missing required fields — fix it and re-run before proceeding.

commands.result_summary:
# Index Context (Context Grounding RAG)

Walkthrough for adding a context resource backed by an ECS Context Grounding index. Used for RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) — the agent issues queries against the index and gets back relevant chunks.

For other context variants, see [context.md](context.md).

## When to Use

- Agent needs to retrieve from a knowledge base of indexed documents
- The index already exists in Context Grounding and is backed by an Orchestrator storage bucket. To create or manage that index from the CLI, see [uipath-platform/references/context-grounding/index-management.md](../../../../../uipath-platform/references/context-grounding/index-management.md)

`uip solution resources refresh` emits an `index` binding into `bindings_v2.json`, resolves the backing storage bucket via ECS + Orchestrator, and writes all three artifacts automatically: `resources/solution_folder/index/<IndexName>.json`, `resources/solution_folder/bucket/orchestratorBucket/<BucketName>.json`, and two `debug_overwrites.json` entries (`kind: "index"`, `kind: "bucket"`). No manual solution-level authoring is required.

**Only `contextType: "index"` with a StorageBucket data source is supported.** `attachments` and `datafabricentityset` contexts, and indexes backed by GoogleDrive / OneDrive / Dropbox / Confluence, emit a warning from refresh and must be hand-authored.

## Discovery

Two `uip` calls — identity from `resource list`, full configuration from `resource get`. Symmetric with [../process/process.md § Discovery](../process/process.md#discovery).

### Step 1 — Verify login and scaffold (if not already done)

Run `uip login status --output json`. If a solution and agent do not yet exist, scaffold per [../../project-lifecycle.md § End-to-End Example](../../project-lifecycle.md#end-to-end-example--new-standalone-agent).

### Step 2 — Find the index (identity)

```bash
uip solution resources list --kind Index --source remote --search "<INDEX_NAME>" --output json
```

Response wrapper: `{Result, Code: "ResourceList", Data: [...]}` — parse `.Data[]`.

| Field | Use as |
|-------|--------|
| `Key` | index GUID — pass to `resource get` in Step 3. Not stored in the agent resource. |
| `Name` | exact `indexName` to set in the context resource → also propagates as binding `name` |
| `Folder` | literal folder path → top-level `folderPath` (e.g., `"Shared/Knowledge"`) and binding `folderPath`. Refresh uses `(name, folderPath)` jointly to look up the index in ECS. |
| `FolderKey` | folder GUID. Refresh resolves it from `Folder`; informational here. |

When the same `Name` repeats across folders, pick by `Key`.

### Step 3 — Get the index configuration

```bash
uip solution resources get <KEY> --output json
```

Response wrapper: `{Result, Code: "ResourceConfiguration", Data: {...}}`. `Data.spec` is the source-of-truth that `uip solution resources refresh` round-trips into `resources/solution_folder/index/<IndexName>.json` — confirm it before authoring.

| `Data.spec` field | Confirms / Use as |
|-------|------------------|
| `dataSourceType` | MUST equal `"StorageBucket"`. Anything else (GoogleDrive / OneDrive / Dropbox / Confluence / Attachments) — refresh warns + skips. Hand-author solution-level files or escalate. |
| `storageBucketReference.name` | Bucket display name. Refresh writes this as the bucket manifest's `name`. Optionally cross-check with `uip solution resources list --kind Bucket --source remote --search "<NAME>" --output json` to confirm the bucket is reachable. |
| `storageBucketReference.key` | Bucket GUID — refresh writes this verbatim as `key` in the bucket manifest and as `dependencies[].key` / `spec.storageBucketReference.key` in the index manifest. |
| `storageBucketReference.folderKey` | Folder GUID containing the bucket. Matches the index's `FolderKey` from Step 2 (the bucket lives in the same folder as the index). |
| `fileNameGlob` | File-extension filter on the index itself. Sanity-check — does not need to match the agent resource's `settings.fileExtension.value`. |
| `includeSubfolders`, `ingestionType`, `encrypted` | Reference fields — refresh round-trips them into the solution-level index manifest. |

Wrapper-level `apiVersion` is `"ecs.uipath.com/v2"` — matches what refresh writes.

## Agent-Level Resource Shape

**Path:** `<AgentName>/resources/<ContextName>/resource.json`

```jsonc
{
  "$resourceType": "context",
  "id": "<uuid>",                       // stable; generate once
  "referenceKey": null,                 // leave null; refresh resolves the ECS index GUID by indexName
  "name": "<ContextName>",              // display name; matches the folder under resources/
  "description": "",
  "contextType": "index",
  "folderPath": "Shared/Knowledge",     // Literal Folder from `uip solution resources list`. Propagates verbatim into bindings_v2.json.
  "indexName": "<IndexName>",           // MUST match the ECS index Name exactly (case-sensitive)
  "settings": {
    "retrievalMode": "semantic",        // "semantic" | "structured" | "deeprag" | "batchtransform"
```
